Sprint 63 (V0.29.17) US-490 DONE (passes:true) 3/4 -- Iris polish P-2, context-aware menu access. THE READING (state it, the AC is ambiguous): AC-1 says the ⋮ shows 'only on the parked/idle home CARD' but its own operative clause says it 'keys off the idle/live STATE', and the goal is 'not reachable by a single accidental tap WHILE DRIVING'. I keyed it to the STATE. While parked there is no driving-tap hazard, so hiding the ⋮ when the operator swipes off the idle card to System Status would cost the affordance and buy no safety. Every safety clause holds under the state reading; the card reading only subtracts. THE LOAD-BEARING PAIR: fail-closed + unconditional override are one design, not two. The unknown side of 'am I driving?' is the DANGEROUS side -> an absent/malformed/idle-less system-status HIDES the tap path (carouselIdle already fails closed; pinned with the truthy string 'true', a bare {}, and a deleted key). That is only safe BECAUSE the 5s hold is state-blind, so I made both flags ONE export -- menuAccess() -> {tapVisible, longPress} -- with a test asserting they DISAGREE while driving. Collapse them into one flag and either the tap returns at 70mph or the override vanishes; that test re-reds either way. SSOT: the US-480-a `idle` boolean, never re-derived from drive.state, pinned in BOTH directions (drive='idle'+idle:false stays hidden; drive='recording'+idle:true shows). THREE LAYERS for AC-4 (never a single tap while driving), because CSS alone is one regression from a clickable target: (1) #menu-btn[hidden]{display:none} stated EXPLICITLY -- #topbar is a FLEX container, so a future `display` on #menu-btn would outrank the UA [hidden] rule silently; (2) the click handler returns early on menuBtn.hidden -- `hidden` the PROPERTY is deliberately the same rendered truth the painter writes, so gate and paint cannot disagree; (3) the button ships hidden in dashboard.html, closing the pre-first-poll unknown window. SCOPE FENCE, TESTED: a guard slices pointerdown..pointercancel and asserts NO menuAccess/tapVisible/carouselIdle/hidden gating leaked into the long-press -- gating the override would lock the operator out in the exact state where they may most need to stop a misbehaving service. CAUGHT MID-FLIGHT, THE REUSABLE LESSON: my first tap-gate guard PASSED against the un-gated code -- the source slice ran on into openMenu/closeMenu and found THEIR `hidden` writes. Any source-inspection guard must be bounded to a window that CANNOT contain an incidental match, and must be watched go red before implementing. A guard that cannot fail is worse than none. WIRING (the cross-file trap, FIFTH sprint running): a pure menuAccess() nobody calls passes every logic test while the ⋮ sits visible at speed -> guard asserts the tick calls updateMenuAccess(sysData), reusing the fetch updateIdleHome already made. AC-3 fences kept: requiresConfirm('stop') true, powerwatch restart-only, Exit still via doAction (no postAction shortcut). NO ATLAS GATE: the conditionalOutcome only fires if the kiosk lifecycle is touched -- allow-list, /service-control, splash hand-off and units are all untouched. GREEN: 17 new; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 216 passed; ruff clean on the touched file (7 I001s in tests/pm/ are PRE-EXISTING, left alone per ruff-scope-discipline). HOST GAP: `make` is not on this box's PATH at all (ran ruff directly) -- black+mypy still not installed either. PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED: parked -> ⋮ visible + opens on tap; start a drive -> ⋮ gone within one poll and ONLY the hold opens the menu; kill the state server -> ⋮ stays hidden, hold still works. Cosmetic: with the ⋮ out of flow the version chip (margin-left:auto) sits at the far right edge while driving -- intended, eyeball it at 480px. NEXT AVAILABLE: US-491 (DTC detail overlay hierarchy, S) -- LAST story in the sprint. Presentation ONLY: directive-first for STOP/WATCH, carded sections, Back >= 40px; ZERO change to severity gating, the S-4 fix-replacement rule, the trust badge or the Mode-04 clear gate. Note US-488 already made .detail-directive tier-driven (data-level -> critical-red/amber/green over a NEUTRAL base) and the tier tag is applied in JS renderDetailBody from view.level -- moving the band must carry that tagging with it or every band silently drops to the neutral base. PRIOR THIS SPRINT: US-489 System Status summary+2x2 grid+dots (three buckets: neutral does not block green, unavailable BLOCKS green but renders muted; fail-closed on unknown levels); US-488 TD-067 sweep 8/10 + the tier-aware directive refactor (2 #clear-confirm surfaces deferred on a --destructive token, TD-067 narrowed not closed). Also open: TD-068 (5 node-probe helpers decode with the locale codepage -- latent until someone asserts non-ASCII copy).
PRIOR NOTE (US-489, kept for the runtime gate): Sprint 63 US-489 DONE (passes:true) 2/4 -- Iris polish P-1, System Status glanceability. THE JUDGEMENT CALL IS THE STORY: a summary line is a LOSSY COMPRESSION of four tiles, so it is exactly where a green-when-broken lie enters -- but the naive reading of AC-1 (green only if all 4 == ok) produces the OPPOSITE dishonesty. DRIVE=IDLE is the only `neutral` this card emits and means 'not recording', not 'broken'; requiring drive==ok makes green UNREACHABLE in the commonest state (key on, no drive started) -> the line reads amber forever and the operator learns to ignore it. Crying wolf is a dishonest instrument too. So: THREE buckets. ok=good; neutral=nominal-inactive (does not block green, is not an issue); unavailable=known-UNKNOWN (BLOCKS green -- never claim OK over a source we cannot read -- but renders MUTED grey, not amber, because nothing is broken); amber/down=the only ISSUES. FAIL-CLOSED on vocabulary: an unrecognised level ranks as unavailable, never ok, so a future tile level cannot paint the card green by default (pinned with a junk level). Line = glanceable COUNT ('SYSTEM · OK' / '· 1 ISSUE' / '· 2 ISSUES' / '· 1 UNAVAILABLE'), detail = the WORST source NAMED ('OBD LINK · RECONNECTING') -- both AC-1 example forms render, and the operator gets count + what-to-look-at without reading four tiles. Worst-wins not first-wins; a real issue always outranks an unknown so an unreadable source can never mask a known fault. SSOT: summary computed from the SAME tiles object the grid renders (test asserts view.summary == systemSummary(view.tiles)) so headline and grid cannot disagree. DOT -- DO NOT 'FIX' THIS: AC-3's parenthetical lists '(green/amber/red/neutral)' but the operative clause is MIRRORING the existing per-tile level, and after US-488/TD-067 there IS no red in this card's mapping. I mirrored faithfully (down->amber) and refused to invent a red dot: it would re-open TD-067 one sprint after I closed 8/10 of it AND contradict the amber number beside it. Test asserts dot and value resolve to the SAME token for `down`. SCOPE FENCE (the trap): appendTile is SHARED with the idle, battery and LTFT cards -> dot is OPT-IN (3rd arg), or three shipped cards restyle from a story scoped to one. Also spelled `.sys-grid .tile:last-child` out explicitly -- the base rule zeroes border-bottom there and the last grid cell would render open-sided. CROSS-FILE CATCH, FOURTH SPRINT RUNNING: grid/dot/summary are classes the JS must EMIT; a CSS-only change styles markup that never renders, silently. Guards assert the renderer emits each class, tags the summary with data-level, and appends the 4 tiles into `grid` and NOT `body`. REAL HARNESS BUG FOUND (not production): the node probe used subprocess text=True with NO encoding, so Python decoded node's UTF-8 with the Windows locale codepage and '·' came back as 'Â·' -- it failed as a one-char diff that looks exactly like a bad production string. Cost me a cycle. Fixed in my file (encoding='utf-8'); 5 sibling helpers share the omission but all their assertions are ASCII so it is LATENT -> filed TD-068 instead of widening the diff. Next person asserting non-ASCII copy gets bitten unless TD-068 lands. GREEN in-loop: 32 new; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 199 passed; ruff clean. black+mypy still not installed on this Windows host (standing gap). PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED (480x320, the card is deliberately re-laid-out): 2x2 must not overflow at 480px with the longest tile values; 17px summary must read at a glance; a parked/OBD-off state must show a MUTED 'SYSTEM · 1 UNAVAILABLE' -- not amber, not green. NEXT AVAILABLE: US-490 (context-aware menu access, S) -- the vertical-dots button shows only on the parked/idle home card, hidden while driving, 5s long-press always. Note it keys off the SAME emitter `idle` SSOT boolean US-481 introduced (carouselIdle in carousel.js) -- do not re-derive idle from the drive-state string.
